sents.t: On Sunday afternoon, we saw the mountains for the first time.
They were the most amazing thing I have ever seen: huge, with snow on the tops, even in May.
At the park entrance, a ranger gave us a map.
“Stay on the trails, and never feed the animals,” she said.
We set up our tent at the campground near a river.
It was harder than I thought, but finally it was standing.
On Monday, we hiked to a lake at the top of a trail.
It was the longest hike of my life, six miles, and the air was thinner, so I got tired quickly.
But the lake was as blue as the sky, and the view was the best in the world.
On the way down, we saw a group of elk eating grass.
Another ranger told us that a big elk can weigh seven hundred pounds!
At night, it was very cold.
We made a campfire, cooked hot dogs, and roasted marshmallows.
Above us, there were millions of stars.
“I’ve never seen the Milky Way before,” I said.
“Neither have I,” Lily said, and she held my hand.
